trust_decision.summary: The per-shell escape function decides which metacharacters are neutralised before an argument is spliced into a shell command; at the pinned commit Zsh left '~' unescaped after '='/':' and after any character, and left '#' and '^' unescaped, so '~' tilde expansion disclosed the user's home path and '^'/'#' re-enabled globbing, while the same class of gap also existed for Dash tilde expansion and for CMD parentheses.

landing_point.why: The advisory names Zsh, and the `specials` regex in Zsh's getEscapeFunction is the list that decides which metacharacters are backslash-escaped; the adjacent `comments`/`expansions` regexes (zsh.js:18-19) are the first thing to read for a tilde/comment/glob gap.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory and its CVE title say Unix/Zsh path disclosure, so the CMD backend under src/internal/win looks like another platform's problem, and Dash/BusyBox look like other shells' problems, none of which the report asks about.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A mid-word tilde must stay literal for Bash, Dash, BusyBox and csh - only a '~' at word start or directly after ':'/'=' is escaped there - whereas the fix switched Zsh to escaping every '~'; copying Zsh's blanket '~' (or a blanket '#'/'^') escape into the other backends breaks their unchanged fixtures.
O5_coupled_behaviour.where: test/fixtures/unix.js:610-631 (bash), test/fixtures/unix.js:1838-1853 (busybox), test/fixtures/unix.js:3098-3113 (csh), test/fixtures/unix.js:4258-4278 (dash); reference rule src/internal/unix/bash.js:19

O6_input_shapes: single metacharacter at word start, middle and end (`~a`, `a~b`, `a~`, `#a`, `a#b`, `^a`)
metacharacter directly after an assignment or path separator (`a=~`, `a:~`, `a=:~:~`, `a==`)
inputs mixed with whitespace, carriage return, U+2028/U+2029, and stripped control characters (`a=~ `, `a=\r:~:`, `a=\u2028:~:`, `a=\u2029:~:`)
inputs whose leading fragments are flag-like (`-`, `--`, `---`, `--a=b`) because the escaper only sees the post-flag substring
CMD parentheses singly and in pairs at start/middle/end (`(a`, `a)b`, `a(b)c`)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Tilde expansion is still escaped only at word start or after whitespace in the BusyBox (ash) backend - byte-identical to the dash gap the fix closes - reachable via Shescape#escape with shell: busybox
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The advisory names Zsh and the fix names Dash; BusyBox ash is a separate shell backend that already carries a '~' guard, so it reads as already covered.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Tilde expansion is still escaped only at word start or after whitespace in the csh backend - the same regex as the dash gap
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: csh is a third shell the advisory never names, with expansion rules that differ from POSIX assignment rules.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the fixed dash rule `(^|[\s:=])~` copied into the BusyBox escaper
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: at the pinned commit busybox.js is a near byte-for-byte copy of dash.js apart from the shell name, so copying the dash fix one file across is the obvious maintainer edit.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the same '(' / ')' addition in cmd's quote-escape `specials` regex
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: cmd.js keeps two parallel specials lists (unquoted at :17 and quoted at :39) and the published fix touched only the first, so a maintainer adding parens would plausibly add them to both.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a '~'- or '#'-style keyword rule for PowerShell's specials2 class
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: powershell.js already splits word-start metacharacters (specials1, :19) from anywhere-in-word ones (specials2, :20), so a neighbouring rule in either class looks natural.

O9_family: shell metacharacter escaping / argument injection (CWE-155 wildcard-or-glob neutralisation, CWE-78 command injection)
